SSGD achieves the same rates as SGD for smooth problems under interpolation, and that the rate of convergence of SSGD for nonsmooth problems under interpolation is the best possible.

(i) SSGD convergences with rates that coincide with the established rates of SGD for smooth problems, (ii) SSGD can achieve these rates even for nonsmooth problems that satisfy an interpolatory condition, and (iii) the convergence rate $O( (1/\epsilon))$, which is optimal for SSGD, coincides with the established rates for SGD applied to smooth interpolation problems
SSGD achieves fast convergence rates in the over-parameterized setting when interpolation holds and that this is optimal in terms of dependence on $\epsilon$.

The main takeaway from our work is that

interpolation is a sufficient condition to guarantee that SSGD has the same convergence rate as SGD for smooth problems, and that the rate $1/\epsilon$ is optimal for the stochastic subgradient method in this setting.
